# ALS Enterprise — Client Presenter Guide & Technical Q&A Manual

**Document Version:** 2.8.0  
**Target Audience:** Lead Presenter, Sales Engineering, Petroleum Operations Leads  
**Platform:** ALS (Artificial Lift Suite) Enterprise Surveillance & Operations Platform  
**Notice:** *DEMO SIMULATED DATA — Telemetry demonstrated is synthetic and generated by high-fidelity nodal mathematical engines without physical wellhead coupling.*

---

## SECTION 1: 5–8 MINUTE EXECUTIVE PRESENTATION SCRIPT

### Introduction & Welcome (1 Minute)
> "Good morning / afternoon everyone. Welcome to the technical demonstration of **ALS Enterprise — the Artificial Lift Operations and Surveillance Suite**.
>
> In unconventional and conventional lift operations today, operating companies face a common set of compounding challenges: premature downhole equipment trips, fragmented surface SCADA systems, lack of visibility into cable degradation, and disconnected field logistics.
>
> ALS was built from the ground up to solve these problems by uniting three mission-critical domains into one responsive, role-governed operational cockpit:
> 1. **High-Density Real-Time SCADA Surveillance** across both surface facilities and downhole gauge strings.
> 2. **Physics-Based Digital Twins** that simulate nodal inflow performance (IPR), fluid drawdown, and thermal degradation live.
> 3. **Closed-Loop Operational Workflows**, including automated alarm triage, a full 8-stage Cable Shop lifecycle, and intelligent fleet dispatch."

---

### Dual-Role Architecture & Fleet Overview (1.5 Minutes)
> "Before diving into the equipment, notice the architectural foundation. The platform features strict role-based access control (RBAC). 
> - **The Administration Portal** provides complete governance over device registries, Modbus tag maps, user permissions, and audit logs.
> - **The User Portal** is engineered as a clean, high-density surveillance cockpit for control-room operators and surveillance engineers.
>
> On the Operations Dashboard, operators have instant visibility into all **20 monitored wells** across our Permian Delaware and Eagle Ford assets. 
> 
> Across the top control room bar, we track 10 critical operational KPIs:
> - **18 Running Wells**, **0 Active Unhandled Trips**, **2 Cycling Wells**, and **1 Telemetry Warning**.
> - **14,320 BPD** total fluid production, alongside active power demand and an average fleet health score of **88.4%**.
> 
> Notice on the left our persistent **Asset Monitoring Selector**. It separates wells into Running, Threat, Down, and No Comm groups. Selecting any asset immediately locks the entire workspace to that well."

---

### SCADA Telemetry & 10 Pressure/Temperature Gauges (1.5 Minutes)
> "Moving into **SCADA Monitoring**, our cockpit unifies 10 critical instrumentation gauges:
> - Downhole: **Pump Intake Pressure (PIP)** and **Pump Discharge Pressure (PDP)**.
> - Casing & Annulus: **A-Annulus Pressure** (sealed casing verification) and **B-Annulus Pressure** (vent line).
> - Surface: **Tubing Head Pressure (THP)**, **Flowline Pressure**, and **Flowline Temperature**.
> - Electrical & Diagnostics: **Motor Temperature**, **Intake Fluid Temperature**, and **RTU Battery Float Voltage**.
>
> Each parameter features dual Imperial/Metric toggles, operating thresholds, and historical sparklines. Operators can also review 7 synchronized trend families — comparing intake pressure against motor temperature and VFD frequency."

---

### Physics-Based Digital Twin (1.5 Minutes)
> "Now let us examine the **Digital Twin**. This is where ALS fundamentally differentiates itself from ordinary SCADA viewers.
>
> In the **Downhole Wellbore Schematic**, the twin renders the full mechanical string from surface down to 11,480 feet:
> - The Phoenix gauge pod, 240 HP motor, protector seal chamber, vortex gas separator, and 182-stage centrifugal pump.
> - Dynamic fluid levels and pressure callouts update live as the well produces.
> - When an engineer adjusts the VFD Frequency Trim slider (for example, stepping from 58.5 Hz down to 56.0 Hz), the built-in affinity law physics solver recalculates the dynamic fluid column, discharge head, and thermal dissipation envelope in real time.
>
> Switching to the **Surface Wellhead / Christmas Tree View**, operators can inspect master valves, swab valves, adjustable chokes, and transmitter manifold connections with full wear-index telemetry."

---

### Cable Shop, Reliability & Logistics (1.5 Minutes)
> "Finally, ALS closes the loop on field maintenance:
> - **ESP Performance**: Multi-frequency H-Q hydraulic curves (35–75 Hz) show exactly where the well operates relative to its Best Efficiency Point (BEP).
> - **Root Cause Failure Analysis**: Pareto analytics identify gas locking (31%) and solids erosion (24%) as primary drivers, benchmarked against MTBF distributions across major manufacturers.
> - **8-Stage Cable Shop Workflow**: Tracks every cable spool through individual testing, DC Hi-Pot verification (15 kV), splicing, shipment preparation, warehouse delivery, and automated invoicing.
> - **Fleet Logistics**: Tracks field maintenance trucks with live GPS, driver Hours-of-Service compliance, and route replay to dispatch nearest crews to well alarms."

## SECTION 3: 12 COMPREHENSIVE CLIENT Q&As

### Q1: How does ALS connect to physical wells, and what protocols are supported?
> **Answer:**  
> In commercial deployments, ALS interfaces with field assets through an industrial edge gateway layer supporting **Modbus TCP/RTU**, **OPC-UA**, **MQTT (Sparkplug B)**, and **WITSML/PRODML** standards. Edge devices deployed on the well pad (e.g. Phoenix, Baker Hughes, or Schneider RTUs) poll downhole gauge mandrels and VFD inverters, package telemetry into lightweight encrypted payloads, and stream them via cellular/satellite backhaul to the ALS enterprise ingestion pipeline.

---

### Q2: What is the telemetry latency from downhole sensor to the control room screen?
> **Answer:**  
> Latency is typically **500 milliseconds to 2 seconds** over high-speed cellular, and **3 to 5 seconds** over satellite links (SCADA polling cycles). For safety-critical interlocks (such as instantaneous underload gas-lock trips or reverse rotation backspin lockouts), protective logic executes locally on the pad RTU or VFD controller at 100 ms cycle speeds, ensuring safety is never compromised by backhaul network latency.

---

### Q3: Does ALS support other forms of artificial lift besides ESPs?
> **Answer:**  
> Yes, ALS is a comprehensive multi-lift platform. The current suite monitors **Electric Submersible Pumps (ESP)**, **Rod Beam Pumping Units** (including surface and downhole dynamometer card diagnostic analysis), **Progressing Cavity Pumps (PCP)** (hydraulic torque monitoring), and **Continuous/Intermittent Gas Lift** (choke differential and injection mandrel rates). The navigation and data schemas seamlessly accommodate mixed-lift fields.

---

### Q4: Can ALS integrate with our existing SCADA host (e.g. CygNet, Wonderware, ClearSCADA)?
> **Answer:**  
> Absolutely. ALS does not require replacing existing field SCADA investments. ALS frequently deploys as an **advanced analytics and digital twin overlay**, consuming telemetry via CygNet Enterprise Bridge REST APIs, OPC-UA servers, or direct Kafka/MQTT message queues. This allows operators to maintain existing field controllers while upgrading control room engineering capabilities.

---

### Q5: How is network security and cybersecurity handled according to the Purdue Industrial Model?
> **Answer:**  
> ALS adheres strictly to ISA/IEC 62443 and the **Purdue Model**:
> - Field instrumentation and drives reside in **Level 1 and 2 (Control & Supervisory Networks)**.
> - The industrial edge gateway sits in **Level 3 (Manufacturing DMZ)** with unidirectional outbound-only TLS 1.3 tunnels.
> - No external network traffic directly accesses the wellhead controllers. All VFD frequency trim commands sent from the User Portal require **two-factor authentication (2FA)** and pass through safety-envelope validation before an authorized write packet is issued.

---

### Q6: Can the autonomous VFD trims cause damage if telemetry is noisy?
> **Answer:**  
> No. The platform employs a strict **Safe Operating Envelope (SOE)** engine with human-in-the-loop interlocks. Every speed change has hard rate-of-change limits (e.g., maximum ±0.5 Hz per 15 minutes) and is constrained by downhole motor temperature, vibration RMS limits (<0.50 G), and minimum pump intake pressure. If telemetry jitter or packet loss is detected, the drive holds its current setpoint and alerts the operator.

---

### Q7: How are the Digital Twin physics models calibrated for specific reservoir fluid properties (PVT)?
> **Answer:**  
> The Digital Twin uses a calibrated **Nodal Analysis solver**. Fluid density, viscosity, water cut, gas-oil ratio (GOR), and bubble point pressure are configured in the Asset Management module. The solver incorporates standing or Beggs-Brill multiphase correlations to determine pressure gradients down the tubing string, ensuring that measured intake pressure accurately correlates with dynamic reservoir fluid levels.

---

### Q8: What business value does the 8-stage Cable Shop workflow provide?
> **Answer:**  
> Downhole ESP cables account for up to **35% of artificial lift capital expenditure**. Without systematic tracking, operators frequently run damaged or improperly spliced cables, resulting in premature electrical failures within 60 days of workover. The 8-stage Cable Shop workflow enforces Hi-Pot testing certification, splice traceability, and spool custody, historically extending average cable run life by **over 120 days**.

---

### Q9: Is the platform accessible on mobile tablets for field pumpers and technicians?
> **Answer:**  
> Yes. The ALS User Portal is fully responsive and optimized for ruggedized field tablets (such as Panasonic Toughbook or iPad Pro). Field personnel can review live well status, acknowledge field alarms, record acoustic fluid levels, and log chemical batches directly from the well plinth.

---

### Q10: What is the typical Return on Investment (ROI) and payback period for ALS?
> **Answer:**  
> In an asset with 100 producing wells:
> - Preventing just **two premature ESP workovers per year** saves approximately **$300,000 to $450,000** in pulling rig and replacement hardware costs.
> - Optimizing VFD frequency to maintain optimal drawdown yields an average **2% to 4% production uplift** across the fleet.
> - Most operator clients realize complete platform investment payback within **4 to 6 months of commissioning**.

---

### Q11: How is multi-operator tenant data isolated, and is the platform SOC2 compliant?
> **Answer:**  
> The backend architecture utilizes tenant isolation with row-level security (RLS) and encrypted database partitions. All customer production figures, reservoir attributes, and well coordinates are protected with AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit. Access logs and setpoint modifications are immutably audited.

---

### Q12: How do we transition from this demonstration prototype to live field deployment?
> **Answer:**  
> The platform is architected for zero-rebuild transition. The frontend UI, state engines, and data schemas remain identical. Moving to production involves two steps:
> 1. Configuring the Edge Gateway IP endpoints in the Admin Device Management module.
> 2. Switching the telemetry ingest driver from the synthetic physics simulation loop to the live Modbus/OPC-UA field stream. A 20-well pilot can be brought live in less than **4 weeks**.
